subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, show that a² cot A + b² cot B + c² cot C = abc/R.

mark_split.label: Convert to sines by the sine rule
Use the identity and convert to abc/R

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Convert to sines by the sine rule
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. a = 2R sinA turns a² cotA into 4R² sin²A · cosA/sinA — and one sine cancels, leaving 2R²(2 sinA cosA), which is a double angle.
steps.memory_tip: a = 2R sinA makes a² cotA into 4R² sin²A · cosA/sinA; one sine cancels, leaving a double angle.
lines: = 4R² sin²A · cosA/sinA + … = 2R²(2 sinA cosA + 2 sinB cosB + 2 sinC cosC)

recall.must_convey: That a = 2R sinA is substituted, one sine cancels against the cotangent, and the result is 2R²(sin2A + sin2B + sin2C).
accept: use a equals two R sin A so a squared cot A becomes four R squared sin A cos A which is two R squared sin two A
the sine rule and then the double angle formula
it becomes two R squared times the sum of sin two A sin two B sin two C
sine rule vaadi sin two A ga marchali
convert the sides and cancel one sine

steps.why: sin²A divided by sinA leaves sinA, which pairs with the cosA to make a double angle. Spotting that cancellation is what keeps the working short.
common_mistakes: Cancelling both sines and losing the double angle.

steps.label: Use the identity and convert to abc/R
steps.margin_note: The other half. sin2A + sin2B + sin2C = 4 sinA sinB sinC in any triangle; then each sine goes back to a side through the sine rule.
steps.memory_tip: Σsin2A = 4 sinA sinB sinC in any triangle; then each sine goes back to a side by the sine rule.
lines: = 2R²(4 sinA sinB sinC)   [∵ in a △, Σsin2A = 4 sinA sinB sinC]

recall.must_convey: That Σsin2A = 4 sinA sinB sinC is quoted, and 8R³ sinA sinB sinC is regrouped as (2R sinA)(2R sinB)(2R sinC)/R = abc/R.
accept: use the identity then regroup eight R cubed sines as a b c over R
each two R sin becomes a side so the product is abc over R
the answer is abc over R
identity vaadi, tarvata sides ga marchali, abc by R
regroup to get the three sides back
heard_as: four sin A sin B sin C

steps.why: 2R²·4 = 8R³/R, and 8R³ sinA sinB sinC is exactly (2R sinA)(2R sinB)(2R sinC) = abc. Splitting the R off is what produces the required form.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as 8R³ sinA sinB sinC.
Re-proving the sin 2A identity instead of quoting it.
